analysis.investment_thesis: Crompton is a solid India consumption play in fans, pumps and appliances — a sector with genuine tailwinds from rising household incomes and electrification. However, net profit has stagnated for four years (617 Cr in FY21 vs 564 Cr in FY25) and revenue CAGR of 9.8% over 7 years is below the 12-15% minimum I demand, making the 34x P/E difficult to justify.
key_strengths: Near debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.05) after aggressively paying down the Butterfly acquisition debt from 1,686 Cr in FY22 to 186 Cr by FY25
Consistent positive OCF across all 5 years reviewed, with FY24 OCF of 843 Cr demonstrating strong cash generation ability
Operating in a structurally growing sector — fans, pumps, kitchen appliances — with India's rising middle class providing 10+ year runway
key_risks: Profit CAGR of only 8.2% over 7 years with net profit still 8% below FY21 levels — no real earnings growth despite revenue expansion, pointing to structural margin pressure
Operating margin of just 8% is thin for a branded consumer electrical company; Butterfly acquisition integration has clearly dragged on profitability
P/E of 34x with sub-10% long-run profit growth offers little margin of safety — stock needs sustained earnings recovery to justify current price
red_flags: No promoter shareholding data — this is a professionally managed company with no founding-family skin in the game, which reduces my confidence in long-term capital allocation
Net profit fell from 617 Cr (FY21) to 442 Cr (FY24) — a multi-year earnings decline in a bull market is a warning sign
Finance costs spiked to 109 Cr in FY23 due to acquisition leverage — reflects capital allocation risk around M&A
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Crompton ticks some important boxes: debt-free, consumer-facing, India-centric product portfolio. The Butterfly Gandhimathi acquisition in 2022 diversified into kitchen appliances but temporarily crushed margins and loaded the balance sheet; the paydown to near-zero debt by FY25 is encouraging and operating profit bounced back strongly in FY25 to 888 Cr. Revenue has grown from 4,804 Cr (FY21) to 7,864 Cr (FY25), a 13% CAGR over four years, which is respectable.

The problem is that earnings power has not followed top-line growth — net profit in FY25 (564 Cr) remains below FY21 (617 Cr), meaning shareholders have waited four years for zero PAT growth. At 34x trailing P/E, you are paying a premium for a recovery story that hasn't yet delivered. Forward P/E of 27x assumes a meaningful earnings step-up; if that materialises in FY26, the stock becomes interesting, but buying at this price requires confident execution that margins will durably recover above 9-10%. I would wait for either a price correction or two consecutive quarters of double-digit PAT growth before adding.
